We have mass spec: m/z 180.0423 (intensity 100) etc. Likely molecular ion at 180.0423. That suggests molecular weight ~180.042. The formula likely C10H12NO2? Let's calculate: C10H12NO2 = 10*12.0000 +12*1.007825 +14.00307 +2*15.99491 = 120 +12.0939 +14.00307 +31.9898 = 178.0868. Not 180.042. C10H13NO2 = 180.094? Let's compute: C10=120, H13=13.1017, N=14.00307, O2=31.9898 total =179.0946? Wait 120+13.1017+14.00307+31.9898=179.09457. Slight off. C10H14NO2 = 180.1024. Our observed 180.0423 is lower by 0.06. Could be C9H10NO3? Compute: C9=108, H10=10.0783, N=14.00307, O3=47.9847 total =180.0661. Slight high. C9H9NO3? H9=9.0704 total =179.0585. Not.

Maybe the ion is [M+H]+? If ESI positive, m/z could be protonated. Then neutral mass = m/z - 1.0073 = 179.035. That matches C10H13NO2 (179.094) still off. C9H11NO3 neutral mass = 179.058? compute C9H11NO3: 108+11.086+14.003+47.985=181.074. Not.

Let's consider exact mass of C10H12N2O? 10*12=120, H12=12.094, N2=28.006, O=15.995 total=176.095. No.

Maybe the ion is [M+Na]+? Then neutral = m/z -22.989 =157.053. Not.

Given carbon NMR peaks: 170.20, 169.60 (likely carbonyl carbons, maybe carboxylic acid and amide). 151.28 (aromatic C attached to hetero). 134.64,132.51,124.01,123.09,122.26 (aromatic carbons). 20.67 (alkyl methyl). So aromatic ring with two carbonyls (maybe amide and carboxylic acid). Methyl attached to carbonyl (acetyl). So structure could be acetanilide with carboxylic acid substituent? That would be p-aminobenzoic acid acetylated? That's acetanilide? Actually acetanilide is C8H9NO, formula 135. Not.

Consider p-acetylaminobenzoic acid? That is acetanilide with carboxylic acid para to amide. Formula: C9? Let's compute: p-acetylaminobenzoic acid (para-aminobenzoic acid with acetyl on N). Base: C7H7NO2 (p-aminobenzoic acid) = C7H7NO2? Actually PABA: C7H7NO2? Wait PABA formula C7H7NO2? Actually PABA is C7H7NO2? Let's compute: C7=84, H7=7.055, N=14.003, O2=31.99 total=137.05. Add acetyl (C2H3O) to N: adds C2H3O (C2=24, H3=3.023, O=15.995) total +43.018 => 180.07. That matches observed 180.042 close. So formula C9? Wait total carbons: 7+2=9? Actually PABA has 7 carbons, plus acetyl adds 2 =9. So C9? But we also have extra carbonyl from carboxylic acid already present. So total carbons = 9? Let's compute: PABA (C7H7NO2) includes benzene (6 C) + carboxyl carbon (1) =7. Add acetyl adds 2 more =9. So formula C9H9? Let's compute full formula: PABA C7H7NO2. Add acetyl (C2H3O) to N (replace H). So new formula: C9H9NO3? Wait we add C2H3O and remove one H from NH2? PABA has NH2 attached to ring. After acetylation, becomes NHCOCH3, so we add C2H3O and lose one H (since NH2 -> NH-). So net addition: C2H2O. So formula becomes C9H9? Let's compute: Starting C7H7NO2. Add C2H2O => C9H9NO3? Actually O count: original O2, add O => O3. H: 7+2=9. N stays 1. So C9H9NO3. Mass: C9=108, H9=9.070, N=14.003, O3=47.985 total =179.058. Protonated would be 180.065. Observed 180.042, close but a bit low. Could be measurement error.

Carbon NMR shows two carbonyls ~170 ppm (carboxylic acid ~170-180, amide ~170). Methyl carbon at 20.67 matches acetyl methyl. Aromatic carbons 6 signals (makes sense). So likely N-acetyl-p-aminobenzoic acid (also known as acetanilide? No that's acetanilide is acetanilide (C8H9NO). This is p-acetylaminobenzoic acid (also called acetanilide? Actually acetanilide is acetanilide (C8H9NO). Not.

Our candidate SMILES: "CC(=O)Nc1ccc(C(=O)O)cc1". That's acetyl amide attached to benzene with carboxylic acid para. That matches our earlier attempt but we got formula C8H9NO? Wait compute: CC(=O)N = acetyl amide group attached to phenyl. The phenyl has carboxylic acid substituent. So total carbons: acetyl (2) + phenyl (6) + carboxyl carbon (1) =9. So C9. Hydrogens: methyl 3, amide NH 1, aromatic hydrogens 4? Actually para substitution reduces to 4 aromatic H. Carboxylic OH 1. Total H =3+1+4+1=9. So C9H9NO3 matches earlier. Good.

Thus SMILES: "CC(=O)Nc1ccc(C(=O)O)cc1". Let's validate.
